scene: A vertical line diagram in grey tones: a wide pipe at the top carries wavy white streaks, a large white arrow pointing down and four black double-headed arrows, then narrows through a funnel-shaped reducer with a white rim into a thin pipe below. The thin pipe is speckled with white bubbles, holds a thinner white down arrow and about five pairs of small black double arrows, and has a hand-lettered label CAVITATION with a short left-pointing arrow beside it.
mechanism: A cross-section diagram of a wide channel squeezing into a narrow one shows the mechanism behind the title's straw idea; no Niagara, waterfall or straw object is drawn, so the title carries the premise.
composition: The artwork is a tall Shorts frame centred in a 16:9 canvas: a white column about a third of the width sits between two flat grey side bars. The funnel at roughly mid height is the focal junction, the narrow pipe runs to the bottom edge, and the label is a small secondary mark on the right of the thin pipe.
typography: One word of tiny hand-lettered black capitals, with no headline anywhere in the frame. CAVITATION is about a hundred pixels wide in a 1280-wide render and is not readable at 160x90, so the title supplies all the semantic information.
colors: Greyscale only: mid-grey fills on a near-white column flanked by darker grey bars, black outlines, white bubbles and arrows. There is no accent colour, so nothing signals emphasis or danger.
psychology: No people or faces appear (the face detector hit in the objective features is not a visible face). The flow arrows and the bubble-filled narrow pipe imply pressure and constriction, but the diagram carries no emotional cue.
partnership: The title poses an absurd what-if about Niagara and a straw, while the image answers a technical aftermath with the word cavitation, which the title never mentions. The sketch implies a consequence without showing the waterfall itself, so the title still does the hooking.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the bright white column on the grey frame first, the big white down arrow in the wide pipe, then the funnel junction, and the tiny CAVITATION label last or not at all.
art: Flat black-outlined marker-style drawing with uniform line weight and consistent grey shading, visibly cropped from a vertical video frame. Dense small arrows and bubbles collapse into texture at phone size, and the two grey side bars waste about two thirds of the width.
strength: The narrowing pipe with a bubble-filled lower section reads as a squeeze at a glance, even at 160x90.
weakness: Pillarboxed vertical art leaves large dead grey bars, and the only word is too small to read on mobile.
bottleneck: The diagram needs the title to make sense because no waterfall, straw or comparison of scale is drawn.
action: Hypothesis: test a version that draws a small waterfall icon above the wide pipe and a straw-width tube below, with a large two-word label, to see whether the mismatch in scale carries the idea alone.
counterexample: Seq 8 is also a near-empty single-object frame but fills the whole canvas with a high-contrast subject, while Seq 1 wastes two thirds of the width.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: STUDENT LOAN BILL / PAYMENT RECEIVED / SKILLED TRADE TECH / THE TRADE WORKS [also a small posted schedule sheet whose lines are too small to read]
scene: A painterly illustration split between two situations. On the left, two figures in black graduation gowns and caps walk across a lawn toward a columned building, one holding a small notebook and one looking down at a phone, while a large printed sheet marked STUDENT LOAN BILL is held in from the bottom-left edge by a hand. On the right, a young man in a dark work shirt with a tool belt holds a phone whose screen reads PAYMENT RECEIVED, with a badge reading SKILLED TRADE TECH, beside an open van whose door shows a clipboard schedule, hanging tools and the van logo THE TRADE WORKS.
mechanism: A before-and-after-style life-path contrast: the loan-bill side versus the paid tradesman side, with the printed signs spelling out the story that the title only labels as POV.
composition: The frame divides roughly at the centre: graduates and loan bill on the left, tradesman and van filling the right half. The tradesman's face and phone are the focal point, the large loan bill is the bottom-left secondary mark, and fine detail across the van interior and the building adds clutter.
typography: No headline overlay. Several short in-scene labels (about eleven distinct words) sit on a paper, a phone screen, a shirt badge and the van; only the large bill title and the van logo are readable at 320x180, and none survive at 160x90, leaving the title as the only strong text.
colors: Warm golden-hour oranges and greens in the background, with dark navy gowns on the left and a dark slate-green work shirt on the right. The cold white of the loan sheet and the paper, plus the bright van interior, are the highest-contrast patches.
psychology: The tradesman has raised brows and wide eyes while looking down at his phone, and the graduates look down with closed mouths. Only these posture and gaze cues are visible; the image is a staged illustration, not a real scene.
partnership: The title promises what happens if you skip college and learn a trade; the image answers with a loan bill against a payment-received notification, which makes the claim visible and partly gives the outcome away. It adds the money-versus-debt framing the title lacks.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the tradesman's face and phone first, then the loan bill in the bottom-left, then the gowned graduates, then the van logo.
art: The raw image is only 360x202 pixels, so it looks soft and fine text is smeared. Lighting is consistent between the two halves, and the figures are anatomically coherent; background figures, signs and tools are small and busy.
strength: Debt and income are visualised as two physical props, a bill and a phone notification.
weakness: Low resolution and no headline mean the key words survive only at the largest sizes, and the van interior is cluttered.
bottleneck: At 160x90 the story relies on tiny colour blocks, so the paper bill and payment screen are not readable.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the tradesman and the loan bill only and add a two-word overlay, to test whether removing the background crowd improves small-size clarity.
counterexample: Seq 3 puts one huge headline on a white background and is readable at phone size, unlike this scene-led frame.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with brown hair, round white glasses with half-lidded eyes and a navy blazer over a white shirt stands at the left edge and points a finger to the right. He points at a small blue-grey safe with a green dial, and a stack of three banded green cash bundles sits beside it. A thick black curved arrow sweeps from under the word RULE down to the safe and cash.
mechanism: A named numerical formula (15 / 65 / 20) is posed as a rule and tied to a safe and cash by a pointing character and an arrow, which makes the specific numbers the hook while leaving what they allocate unexplained.
composition: The man's head fills about half of the frame height on the left; the heavy headline takes the right and upper-centre; the safe sits low-centre. The arrow runs from the headline down to the safe, forming a diagonal read from words to object, and white space keeps the three elements separate.
typography: Five tokens in three stacked lines of heavy black condensed capitals, with the numerals 15 / 65 / 20 much larger than THE and RULE. Contrast on white is maximal, the numerals are readable at 160x90, and the numbers add what the title (The Money Formula the Rich Actually Use) lacks.
colors: Black on pure white with a navy blazer, a pale skin tone and one small green accent in the cash and safe dial. The green is the only saturated element and marks the money.
psychology: Half-closed eyelids and a pointing arm give an unhurried, instructive pose, with no alarm or urgency cue. Gaze is straight ahead rather than toward the safe.
partnership: The title says there is a formula the rich use; the thumbnail supplies the three numbers but not what each refers to, so the open question is what the percentages divide. The thumbnail adds specificity rather than repeating the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the numerals 15 / 65 / 20 first, then the cartoon man's face, then the arrow tip, then the safe and cash.
art: Flat vector cartoon with thick outlines and a clean white canvas. The man is a stock-style character with a tiny body in the crop; the safe and cash are simple clip-art shapes, so the frame reads quickly but looks generic.
strength: Three large numerals set a specific, curiosity-inducing formula that survives at phone size.
weakness: The pointing man and safe are generic props that do not explain what the percentages split.
bottleneck: Viewers cannot tell what the numbers allocate, which is also the curiosity gap, so the label has to do all the work.
action: Hypothesis: add a tiny category label under each number, such as SAVE or SPEND, and compare against the bare numbers to test whether clarity beats mystery.
counterexample: Seq 24 is also white-background money art but an hourglass scene tells a story, where this row relies on a bare numeric formula.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A glossy orange faceless humanoid with two white oval eyes, a white dumbbell icon on the forehead, a defined muscular torso and teal shorts stands at the left edge and points a finger at the first of three food items. Plate one holds three fried eggs, a mound of scrambled egg, a small bowl of oatmeal with berries and a banana. Plate two holds grilled chicken slices, broccoli and rice. The third item is a bowl of yogurt topped with about a dozen blueberries.
mechanism: The three meals are shown as concrete food portions in a left-to-right row, so a viewer sees what the title's three boring meals are and the headline numbers them.
composition: The orange figure takes the left third and is the dominant mass; three food dishes of similar size run in a row across the lower middle, and the headline sits in a row across the top. The row is even and uncluttered on a pale background.
typography: Three words in bold black capitals, each in its own white box with a soft drop shadow, placed along the top right. The headline is large and survives at 160x90, but it merely numbers and categorises the meals and adds no claim beyond the title.
colors: Saturated orange body against a near-white background, with yellow eggs and banana, green broccoli and blue berries as small colour accents. Teal shorts echo the blueberries, and the white boxes give the black text top contrast.
psychology: The figure has no face, only blank oval eyes, and points at the food. It signals demonstration and expertise-by-pose, with no warning, urgency or emotional expression.
partnership: The title calls them boring and says they build every muscle; the thumbnail answers the what by showing the three meals, which satisfies the question early. The word boring is not carried, so the bored-versus-effective tension is lost.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the orange muscular figure first, then the boxed headline, then the egg plate being pointed at, then the chicken and rice plate and the yogurt bowl.
art: Glossy 3D-style character with smooth plastic-like shading composited with flat-vector food plates, so the rendering styles differ between figure and meals. The food items are clearly recognisable and fingers are coherent; the pale background is empty.
strength: Three clean, recognisable food groups in an even row make the promise instantly concrete.
weakness: Showing the meals gives away the answer and drops the word boring from the title's tension.
bottleneck: Because the dishes are fully revealed, the remaining curiosity rests on why these meals work.
action: Hypothesis: blur or silhouette one of the three plates and add a question mark to test whether partial reveal raises curiosity without losing clarity.
counterexample: Seq 8 withholds nearly everything and shows only one blank object, the opposite of this thumbnail's complete reveal.
medical_notes: Nutrition packaging shows ordinary foods with no cure, diagnosis or medication claim.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with dark spiky hair greying at the temples, a navy polo shirt and a small closed-mouth smile holds two large glass jars stuffed with green banknotes and gold coins, his eyes glancing to the right. To the right a green stopwatch icon sits above a stepped pyramid of about five rows of green banknotes, and a thick black curved arrow points down toward the pile from the right edge.
mechanism: The $1,000 amount is turned into physical jars and a pile of notes capped with a stopwatch, which makes the abstract idea of trading money for time visible.
composition: The man and his jars occupy the left half; the headline spans the top; the stopwatch above the bank-note pyramid forms a second focal cluster at lower right, and the arrow ties the two. The balance is two-sided, with a slight diagonal from man to the stack.
typography: Six tokens in two lines of heavy black capitals, with TIME! in larger bright green. The dollar figure and the green word survive at 160x90, while the line BUYING BACK is smaller; the thumbnail adds the buying-back-time angle that the title does not have.
colors: Black headline on white, navy shirt, and lots of bright dollar green repeated across jars, pile, stopwatch and the word TIME. The yellow-gold of the coins gives a warm secondary accent.
psychology: The man's eyes glance sideways and his mouth is closed with a slight upturn; no alarm, fear or hope is signalled beyond the money props. The pose is calm and showcase-like.
partnership: The title asks what actually happens when you invest $1,000 a month; the thumbnail gives the answer as buying back time, which reframes the number as freedom and may pre-empt the click question. The dollar amount is repeated from the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the dollar figure at the top first, then the green word TIME!, then the stopwatch above the notes, and the man's glancing face and jars last.
art: Clean flat-vector cartoon with consistent outlines; both jars and the note pile are drawn with matching green notes. The background is plain white and nothing blends awkwardly, though the arrow pointing at the pile is redundant.
strength: The green TIME! plus stopwatch icon forms a clear one-word concept against the dollar number.
weakness: Every element repeats the money theme, so the jars, pile and arrow compete without one dominant picture.
bottleneck: The thumbnail resolves the question of what investing does, leaving little unanswered besides how.
action: Hypothesis: remove the arrow and one jar and enlarge the stopwatch, to test whether a single time-for-money image beats the multi-prop layout.
counterexample: Seq 23 also uses a money prop and arrow but with a person carrying a sack, which tells a story of effort rather than a showcase of cash.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A grassy cartoon field under a blue sky with a row of pine trees behind. At the left a shaggy brown-haired cave-dweller figure in a fur garment holds a grey rock in one hand with a flat mouth and lowered brows. At the centre a white-headed stick figure with wide eyes and two sweat drops puts a hand to its chin beside a red question mark. At the right a cloth-like map of Europe in red, blue, yellow and green has a black flag on a pole.
mechanism: A timeline-collision visual puts a prehistoric figure, a confused modern stick figure and a political map in one scene, and the question headline asks who started borders.
composition: A three-part horizontal row: caveman left, stick figure at centre as the focal point, map right, with the headline filling the top band. The stick figure's large head and the red question mark pull the eye to the middle; trees and horizon keep the background calm.
typography: Five words in one line of thick-outlined yellow capitals spanning nearly the full width, with a dark outline for contrast against sky blue. The line stays legible at 160x90, and it adds a question that differs from the title.
colors: Saturated sky blue and grass green frame the yellow headline, with the map's red, blue and yellow giving small high-chroma patches. The red question mark is the single strongest accent against the blue sky.
psychology: The stick figure shows wide eyes, a hand on its chin and sweat drops, which signal puzzlement. The caveman has lowered brows and a flat mouth while holding a rock.
partnership: The title asks Who Invented Countries?; the thumbnail rephrases to the first border and shows a map, so the two are close but not identical. The caveman with a rock suggests an answer path without stating it, leaving the who unanswered.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the sweating stick figure with the red question mark, then the caveman with the rock, then the map on the right.
art: Flat doodle-style 2D art with uniform black outlines and a simple three-band background. Characters are cartoons or stick figures, the map is hand-drawn with irregular coastline, and the layout is clear at phone size.
strength: A confused stick figure between a rock-holding caveman and a map tells a one-glance puzzle story.
weakness: The map and flag are fairly small and busy, and the headline spends the top fifth of the frame.
bottleneck: The caveman and map have similar visual weight, so the viewer must decide which one answers the question.
action: Hypothesis: enlarge the map and have the caveman draw a line on it, to test whether showing the action beats the static pose.
counterexample: Seq 14 uses a similar yellow headline over a stick figure but has a more direct comparison between two animals.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: SENIORS STOP! / THIS PAIN PILL / CAUSES / HEART / ATTACKS!
scene: A close-up of a man with a shaved receding hairline, grey beard and mustache, a white coat over teal scrubs and a stethoscope, with a flat closed mouth and slightly furrowed brows looking at the viewer. He holds an amber pill bottle with a white cap, filled with white tablets, in one hand while his other hand points a finger up from the lower left. A red arrow with a white outline points from the headline area at the bottle.
mechanism: A named audience (seniors), a command (stop), an unnamed drug and a catastrophic outcome are combined with a coated figure holding the pills, so the claim and the culprit are tied in one frame.
composition: The headline takes the left 60 percent of the frame in stacked lines, with HEART ATTACKS as the largest block, and the man's head and the pill bottle take the right. The red arrow runs from the headline toward the bottle, and the face is a large secondary focal point.
typography: Eight words in a purple banner (SENIORS STOP!) plus gold-gradient capitals with white CAUSES between them, HEART and ATTACKS! at maximum size. The three big words survive at 160x90. The title says may affect your heart, so the thumbnail strengthens the claim to causes.
colors: Dark purple on the left, orange-to-red gradient behind the man, and gold-yellow lettering with a white word and a red arrow. The palette is saturated and high-contrast, with red and yellow signalling alarm.
psychology: The man looks directly at the viewer with a flat mouth and creased brows while holding the bottle, which reads as serious or cautionary. The white coat and stethoscope are authority cues, though no name or credential is printed.
partnership: The title hedges that the painkiller can affect the heart after 60, while the thumbnail states that the pill causes heart attacks, a stronger and less qualified claim. The pill is unnamed in both, which leaves which painkiller as the open question.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: HEART ATTACKS in gold first, then the man's stern face, then the red arrow and pill bottle, then the purple SENIORS STOP! banner.
art: Photo-like face and hands composited on a gradient background with a stylised arrow and text. The bottle label is blank and the coat and scrubs are coherent; the lighting on the face is flat but there are no clear artefacts, so no synthetic claim is made.
strength: HEART ATTACKS in huge gold capitals is readable at 160x90 and pairs with a large face and pill bottle.
weakness: The claim that the pill causes heart attacks is stronger than the title and names no drug or dose.
bottleneck: Alarm styling and the stethoscope are visible, but the medical authority is not tied to any printed name or credential.
action: Hypothesis: replace CAUSES with CAN RAISE RISK OF and name the drug class in small text, to test whether a calibrated claim holds attention while matching the title.
counterexample: Seq 16 uses calm teal and a smiling clinician with a neutral definition question, the opposite tone of this alarm layout.
medical_notes: The thumbnail states that an unnamed pain pill causes heart attacks while the title says it can affect the heart, and the white-coat figure carries no printed credential.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A single black-outlined drawing of a white marshmallow, a short cylinder with slightly bulging sides and an oval top face, sits alone at the centre of a flat cyan background. Nothing else is visible: no people, no text, no arrows.
mechanism: The title's one noun is drawn as a lone object, so the thumbnail acts as an iconic label rather than a story.
composition: The object is dead centre and fills about 55 percent of the frame height, with large empty cyan margins on either side. Hierarchy is trivial because only one element exists, and the edges are quiet.
typography: No text of any kind. The title, which is three words, supplies every word, and the image only illustrates the central noun.
colors: Two-colour scheme of saturated cyan and white with black outlines. The white form is separated from the cyan by a thick black contour, and there is no warning or accent colour.
psychology: No face, gaze or gesture is shown. The simple blank form conveys neutrality, so curiosity has to come from the title's reference to a known experiment.
partnership: The title names the Marshmallow Effect and the image shows only a marshmallow, so the picture repeats the key noun without adding a child, a choice or a delay. It offers no unanswered question beyond the title's own.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white shape against cyan is the only thing seen, with the black outline read second and nothing else to scan.
art: Hand-drawn marker-style outline with slight wobble and flat fills on a gradient-free cyan background. It is clean and extremely simple, and fully legible at 160x90, but it carries almost no visual information.
strength: One clear object on a saturated flat colour is instantly legible even at the smallest size.
weakness: The frame shows nothing beyond a marshmallow, with no person, choice or tension to suggest the effect.
bottleneck: Without any text or story element the thumbnail depends entirely on the title for meaning.
action: Hypothesis: add a second tiny marshmallow and a hand reaching for it, to test whether a visible temptation moment adds interest to the bare icon.
counterexample: Seq 6 fills a comparable flat-colour scene with three story elements and a question headline, the opposite of this minimal frame.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: doomed / by fate [small round logo at top left reading lost LEGACY]
scene: A cartoon gladiator with a big round tan head, spiky blond hair, small stitch-like marks and scuffs on one cheek, a lowered brow and a wavy pink mouth leans in from the left edge. He wears a segmented grey shoulder guard, holds a sword hilt at the bottom left and has a red rectangular shield with gold laurel sprigs in front of his torso. A thin hand-drawn arrow curves from beneath the words toward the shield.
mechanism: A downcast cartoon fighter is paired with a fatalistic phrase, so the thumbnail frames the gladiator's life as hopeless without showing any arena or fight.
composition: The character fills the left 45 percent and is cropped at the top and bottom edges, while the two-line text takes the right half in the vertical middle. The thin arrow runs from the lower text toward the shield, linking text to figure, and the empty white space around both gives a very low-clutter layout.
typography: Three lowercase words in a rounded hand-drawn black font, set in two lines at a size comparable to the head. High contrast on white keeps them readable at 160x90. The phrase adds a fatalistic angle that the title's Why It Sucked to Be a Gladiator does not state.
colors: White canvas with a tan face, a pale-yellow haircut and a saturated red shield whose gold laurels make small accents. The red shield is the strongest colour patch and separates the body from the background.
psychology: Visible cues are a furrowed brow, small side-glancing eyes and a wobbly downturned mouth, with marks on the face. Together they read as weary or worried, matching the doom wording.
partnership: The title promises why the life was awful and the thumbnail answers with a fate framing, which supplies a mood but no reason. The unanswered question is what exactly made the job miserable.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red shield and large worried face first, then the lowercase phrase doomed by fate, and the arrow and small corner logo last.
art: Flat cartoon outlines with a hand-drawn marker feel and soft flat shading. The figure is clearly cropped, shield and armour are coherent, and the white space makes the frame readable on mobile despite the thin arrow.
strength: A big downcast face and a bold red shield tell the mood at a glance without any busy background.
weakness: The phrase states fate but names neither the gladiator job nor a concrete reason for the misery.
bottleneck: The thin arrow is the weakest element at 160x90, so the connection between the words and shield is not obvious.
action: Hypothesis: replace the thin arrow with a thick one or remove it, and change the text to name the job such as DOOMED GLADIATOR, to test whether naming the subject lifts clarity.
counterexample: Seq 15 shows the same cartoon-history idea with an explicit expectation panel and a reality panel, so the cause of misery is visible instead of implied.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A cartoon man with red-orange hair, a grey T-shirt, blue jeans and brown shoes stands at the left holding open an empty brown wallet in both hands, his mouth open and eyes cast up and to the right. About seven green dollar bills fly away from the wallet in a trail toward a large gold trophy topped with a globe and held up by two sculpted figures at the right. A thick black curved arrow sweeps from the headline down toward the trophy.
mechanism: Cash visibly leaves an empty wallet and flows to a trophy, so the thumbnail depicts event spending as a drain on the viewer's money.
composition: The man takes the left third and the gold trophy the right third, with the flying bills forming a diagonal bridge between them. The headline fills the upper right, and the arrow turns the eye back down to the trophy.
typography: Three words in two lines of heavy black condensed capitals with a question and exclamation mark, the second line YOU?! larger. Contrast on white is maximal, and the large size keeps it legible at 160x90. It names the consequence while the title adds the event context.
colors: Black headline and outline on white, saturated dollar green on the bills, and the glossy gold of the trophy as the brightest accent. The man's grey shirt and blue jeans stay muted, so the money and trophy dominate.
psychology: The man's open mouth, wide eyes and raised glance signal surprise or dismay, and the empty wallet reads as loss. The headline's question and interrobang address the viewer directly.
partnership: The title promises a spending trap about the World Cup and the thumbnail shows the trophy and the vanishing money, which makes the topic concrete. The headline says draining you, while the title adds nobody talks about it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the headline YOU?! first, then the man's surprised face and wallet, then the flying bills toward the golden trophy, then the arrow.
art: Flat vector cartoon in a stock-style look, with thick outlines and a clean white background. The trophy is a more detailed gradient-shaded object than the character, and nothing overlaps awkwardly.
strength: The empty wallet to flying money to trophy sequence reads left to right in one glance.
weakness: The cartoon man and arrow are stock-style staples that look similar to other money thumbnails.
bottleneck: The idea of a trap is implied by a plain money loss, so distinct stakes are missing.
action: Hypothesis: add a visible price figure on the trophy or a ticket stub to test whether a concrete cost makes the drain more specific.
counterexample: Seq 3 uses a similar character-plus-arrow layout but puts numerals instead of a loss scene in the headline, so it leans on specificity rather than loss.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: Your Brain / Hides 95% / of Your Dreams
scene: Against a black background, a white line drawing of a head in left-facing profile contains a brain outline. One strip along the back-right edge of the brain is filled solid red; the rest of the brain is left empty black. A white arrow with a curved shaft points up from the bottom left toward the chin and neck of the head, and the headline occupies the left half.
mechanism: A diagram where only a small red slice of the brain is highlighted illustrates the hidden-dream claim, with the red numerals tying the percentage to the picture.
composition: The three-line headline fills the left 55 percent and the head profile the right 45 percent, centred vertically. The red brain strip is a small secondary accent, and the white arrow in the lower left leads the eye toward the neck rather than the brain.
typography: Seven words in three stacked lines of clean white sans-serif, with 95% and Dreams in red. Contrast against black is maximal and all three lines remain readable at 160x90. The text repeats the title word for word and adds no new information.
colors: Pure black background with white lines and text, and red used for the 95% numerals, the word Dreams and the brain strip. The restricted palette makes the red words stand out strongly.
psychology: The head is an empty outline with no eyes or expression, so nothing is conveyed by gaze or pose. The red highlight and the bold percentage supply the only emotional intensity.
partnership: The thumbnail text is the title nearly verbatim, so the image adds only the head diagram. The highlighted brain strip is a small share, which does not obviously match the 95 percent figure and leaves the unanswered question of what is hidden and why.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the red 95% first, then the large white words Your Brain, then the head outline with the red brain strip, and the arrow last.
art: Minimal vector line art on pure black with consistent stroke weight and no gradients. It looks tidy and diagram-like, and every element holds up on mobile, though the arrow's target is unclear.
strength: Red numerals and words on a black background make 95% and Dreams stand out clearly.
weakness: The text repeats the title exactly, and the arrow points at the neck rather than at the highlighted brain region.
bottleneck: Little new information is added beyond the title, so the thumbnail does not extend the curiosity.
action: Hypothesis: shade 95 percent of the brain red and leave a small unshaded part, or aim the arrow at it, to test whether the picture matching the number improves comprehension.
counterexample: Seq 13 uses a one-question headline plus a concrete scene that changes the angle of the title, while this row only restates it.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

scene: A snowy park path with frosted grass and a frosted shrub at the far right. At the left a figure in a grey-green greatcoat and steel helmet walks toward the camera under a yellow label reading SPY. At the right two figures in peaked caps and dark uniforms sit side by side on a wooden park bench, and a white-on-black tag reading HITLER points down at the right-hand seated figure.
mechanism: The two printed labels turn a quiet wintry bench scene into an implied secret encounter, so the viewer must work out why the walker is called a spy.
composition: The walking figure is on the left third and the bench pair at the right-centre, with a wide pale-snow gap between them that creates a diagonal tension. The two labels sit high in the frame at different heights, and the desaturated snow keeps the colour figures isolated.
typography: Two single-word tags, a yellow SPY with black letters and a black HITLER with white letters, each with a small downward pointer. Contrast is strong and both survive at 160x90. They label people rather than make a claim and echo the nouns in the title.
colors: Near-greyscale white-grey snow and grass with olive-grey uniforms, brown bench slats and a small red band on the caps and trousers. The one yellow tag is the only saturated colour.
psychology: The standing figure looks ahead with a neutral mouth, and the seated figures look down at the ground with hands on knees. Only these body cues are visible; the scene is quiet rather than overtly threatening.

partnership: The title says that being an emperor was miserable, and the thumbnail shows the cause as violent threat from his own guards, which is a concrete reason. It reveals the core angle early, leaving the how and why of the guards' turn open.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the gold EXPECTATION word first, then the calm character on the throne, then the red REALITY word, then the swords and soldiers around the shocked emperor.
art: Hand-inked cartoon with muted shading and consistent character design across both panels. The swords, helmets and furniture are coherent and the right panel has a busier background, but the central figures stay clear at phone size.

psychology: The man's sideways glance, downturned mouth and slightly raised brows read as doubt. The animals look calmly at the viewer or sideways.
partnership: The title says humans mostly drink cow's milk, while the thumbnail shows a group of other milking animals and no cow, which supplies a visual set of alternatives. The missing cow is the unexplained gap.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow headline first, then the man holding the dripping bowl, then the cluster of animals on the right, with the cups last.
art: Flat cartoon with thick outlines and layered scenery. The animals are drawn at believable relative scale and overlap tidily; the many small details at the right (cups, fence, hooves) merge at 160x90, but the headline and main figure stay clear.
strength: One person and five different milk animals make an immediate set of alternatives to cow milk.
weakness: The five animals are similar in visual weight and sit in a tight cluster, so no one animal anchors the answer.

scene: A cartoon man with short black hair, round glasses and a navy suit sprawls back in a brown armchair with wide eyes, an open mouth and a sweat drop on his forehead and cheek. A thick brown fuzzy coil loops across his chest and shoulder. A grey flexible vacuum hose with a nozzle presses against his jacket, sucking up green banknotes and gold coins that spill from his pocket and chest.
mechanism: A relaxed man in an armchair is literally being vacuumed of his money, which turns the abstract idea that comfort drains wealth into a physical gag.
composition: The huge headline spans the top, and the man and chair fill the lower two thirds with the head at the top centre. The vacuum hose curving out to the lower right leads the eye along a diagonal, and the top of his head touches the bottom edge of the headline.
typography: Three words in one line of very tall condensed black capitals stretching edge to edge. High contrast on white, readable at 160x90, with the verb KILLS giving a dramatic claim. The title says convenience premium and paying double, while the thumbnail names comfort and wealth.
colors: Black headline on white, a warm brown chair and fuzz, a navy suit and a green cash accent, with sweat drops in pale blue. The green bills at the nozzle are the only saturated detail and mark the leak.
psychology: The wide eyes, open mouth and sweat drops are clear alarm cues, and the sprawled pose suggests loss of control. The contrast between a cosy chair and a panicked face drives the emotion.
partnership: The title says convenience costs double for laziness, and the thumbnail personifies the idea as a comfy chair draining cash. It adds a vivid image but changes the keyword from convenience to comfort, leaving the specific premium unexplained.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the giant black headline first, then the man's panicked face under it, then the vacuum nozzle and flying cash at the lower right.
art: Flat vector cartoon with thick outlines and clean fills. The brown fuzzy coil across the chest has an unclear identity, and the hose and chair overlap the body in a slightly cluttered way, though the main face and headline remain clear.
strength: A vacuum hose pulling cash out of a jacket pocket is a simple, memorable visual metaphor.
weakness: The unexplained furry coil wrapped around the man clutters the centre and does not tie to a money idea.
bottleneck: The headline's claim is abstract and the metaphor only partly maps to convenience.

text: FLUSH / 13 LBS / of GUT WASTE / IN 1 MINUTE
scene: On a dark blurred navy background, a large orange-red illustration of the large and small intestine fills the left, with the lower colon cut open to show a mass of brown clumps. At the right a woman with shoulder-length grey-blond hair squeezes her eyes shut and grimaces while both hands press her belly, which carries an orange-red glow. A thin yellow curved arrow runs from her abdomen to the opened colon.
mechanism: A quantified purge claim (13 pounds in one minute) is linked by an arrow and a glowing abdomen to an anatomical colon full of clumps, so the thumbnail shows both a number and its supposed container.
composition: The anatomy illustration takes the left 40 percent, the stacked headline sits in the centre and the woman is cropped at the right edge. The yellow arrow sweeps from the lower right toward the opened colon, creating a loop from headline to body, and the dark ground keeps everything separated.
typography: Nine tokens in four lines: white FLUSH, large yellow 13 LBS, smaller white of with yellow GUT WASTE, then white IN 1 MINUTE. The top two lines survive at 160x90 while the lower lines shrink. The number and time claim are not in the title.
colors: A near-black navy ground with saturated orange-red organs, brown waste clumps, bright yellow numerals and a yellow arrow. The red glow on the abdomen and the red anatomy are used as pain and alarm signals.
psychology: The woman's closed eyes, tight grimace and hands pressed to the belly signal pain or distress, and the red glow underlines it. The medical illustration and large numeral add a shock element.
partnership: The title promises a one-minute bedtime drink and waste coming out in the morning, while the thumbnail claims 13 lbs of waste flushed in one minute, which is a different and stronger claim. The drink itself is not shown at all.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the yellow 13 LBS first, then the clumped colon illustration, then the woman's grimace and glowing belly, then the small lower lines of text.
art: A smooth anatomical render is combined with a photo-style portrait and flat text and arrow overlays on a blurred dark backdrop. The intestine illustration has a glossy plastic look and the woman's lighting differs from the illustration, so the two read as a composite.
strength: A large yellow 13 LBS numeral and a clumped colon give a stark, instantly legible claim.
weakness: The dramatic claim of 13 lbs in one minute is stronger than the title and implies a purge outcome with no source.
bottleneck: The pain image plus the waste picture can mislead, and the bedtime drink named in the title is missing.
action: Hypothesis: replace the colon with a glass of the drink and remove the numeric weight claim, to test whether a plain product shot reduces the exaggerated impression while keeping curiosity.
counterexample: Seq 16 is the calm contrast: no numeric claim, no pain imagery, and a smiling clinician on teal.
expression_label: eyes shut, grimace, hands on belly
medical_notes: The thumbnail claims 13 lbs of gut waste flushed in 1 minute and pairs a pained abdomen with a colon packed with clumps, which is a stronger and unsourced claim compared with the title.

text: THE BILLIONAIRE TRAP / 95% END UP BROKE / COPY ME! / MY SECRETS [on each of two books] / THE OTHER 95% / SUCCESS!
scene: At the left, a cartoon man in a black suit and sunglasses stands on a gold podium labelled SUCCESS! under a spotlight, holding up two gold books each marked MY SECRETS with a banner reading COPY ME! over his head, while bills and coins fall around him. At the centre a crowd in grey tones, eight clearly visible in front and about six more heads behind, stand or sit looking down at empty open wallets under a label THE OTHER 95%. At the right a man in a navy suit and glasses pulls a red curtain aside, and a red arrow points from him at the crowd.
mechanism: A survivorship-bias scene: a spotlighted winner is shown on a podium while a curtain is pulled back to reveal a large downcast crowd, which restates the headline's 95 percent claim.
composition: Three zones run left to right: the lit winner, the grey crowd and the curtain man, with the two-line headline above them. The red arrow and curtain point inward toward the crowd, but the many labels, books, coins and faces compete for attention.
typography: About seventeen words across a two-line black headline with red TRAP and 95%, plus four in-scene labels. The top headline survives at 160x90, while COPY ME!, the book titles and THE OTHER 95% do not. The COPY ME! banner crowds the lower edge of the 95% in the second line.
colors: Black headline on white with red accents on TRAP, 95%, the arrow and the curtain, a yellow spotlight and gold podium on the left, and a desaturated grey-blue crowd. The red marks danger while the grey crowd reads as sad or muted.
psychology: The crowd members look down at empty wallets with downturned faces, while the winner has a wide grin with arms raised. The curtain man looks toward the viewer with a flat mouth.
partnership: The title is about a famous billionaire's morning routine not making you rich, while the thumbnail turns it into a billionaires-versus-everyone-else story with a 95 percent statistic that the title does not state. No routine or named person is shown.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black THE BILLIONAIRE TRAP headline first, then the red 95% and the red arrow, then the spotlit winner, then the grey crowd.
art: Flat vector cartoon with grey-toned background characters and a bright foreground winner. The layout is dense with overlapping figures, books, labels and falling money, and the headline lines sit close above the artwork.
strength: The spotlight-versus-crowd contrast gives the survivorship idea an immediate before-the-curtain reveal.
weakness: Around seventeen words and many small labels crowd the frame, and most of the in-scene text disappears at phone size.
bottleneck: With the headline, four labels, a crowd and a podium all competing, no single image anchors the idea at 160x90.
action: Hypothesis: cut the crowd to three figures and remove the book and banner labels, to test whether a simpler version holds attention at small size.
counterexample: Seq 24 tells a similar money-trap story with a single hourglass subject and two text blocks, so it reads far faster.
evidence_labels: text,scene=DATA; diagnostic fields and scores=INFERENCE; proposed changes=HYPOTHESIS

text: FAKE PREMIUM / MARKETING TRICK / GENERIC VODKA [tiny garbled lettering on the bottle neck]
scene: On a grey stone-like surface against a dark navy backdrop with faint light rays, a frosted glass bottle with a blue cap glows from within and carries a goose-like bird graphic and a snowy mountain scene. A bright blue hand peels back a silver foil sticker at the lower part of the bottle, uncovering a plain white label that reads GENERIC VODKA. A red speech-bubble badge to the right of the bottle reads MARKETING TRICK.
mechanism: A premium bottle is shown mid-unmasking, with a sticker peeled off to reveal a generic label, so the headline's fake claim has a physical proof moment.
composition: The bottle stands at the centre as the focal point, the huge headline spans the upper third and the red badge sits at the middle right. The blue hand at the lower right pulls the eye along a diagonal toward the peeled label, and the bottle cap and neck sit in front of the letter R in PREMIUM.
typography: Six words in two white heavy sans-serif lines at the top, the badge in white on red, and a small label on the bottle. FAKE PREMIUM and the red badge survive at 160x90 while GENERIC VODKA is small. The text adds a brand-exposure angle that the title expresses as brilliant lie.
colors: Dark navy with a cold blue glow, pure white headline, a vivid red badge as the only warm accent and a bright blue glove. The red badge works as an alarm, and the pale bottle pops against the dark ground.
psychology: There are no faces; the cues are the peeling motion, the red alarm badge and the dramatic rim lighting. The hand gesture signals exposure.
partnership: The title says a famous brand fooled millions with one brilliant lie, while the thumbnail shows the lie as a stripped label with generic vodka, which gives the answer in picture form. The brand is not printed, so the audience relies on the title to name it.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the white FAKE PREMIUM headline first, then the glowing bottle, then the red MARKETING TRICK badge, then the blue hand and the peeled label.
art: Photoreal bottle render with soft rim light and a smooth gradient backdrop. The small lettering on the bottle neck is garbled and does not form real words, and the all-blue hand looks flat next to the glossy glass, so some elements look synthetic or composited.
strength: The peeled sticker revealing GENERIC VODKA is a clear before-the-lie visual in one gesture.
weakness: The bottle neck letters are garbled and the bottle is only a partial lookalike, which weakens credibility.
bottleneck: The headline and badge both carry the debunking idea, so the picture reveals the answer before the title is read.
action: Hypothesis: crop to the peeling sticker only and remove the red badge, to test whether the single reveal beats the doubled FAKE and MARKETING TRICK messaging.
counterexample: Seq 8 leaves the viewer with only an unlabelled object, while this row spells out the debunking in two text pieces.

composition: The man and sack fill the left half in a diagonal leaning pose, the stairs lead up toward the headline, and the three words stack on the right half. The red arrow at the bottom sits on the stair line and points toward the last word.

colors: Black text on white, a sandy-beige sack, a pale blue shirt and a navy trouser, with the red arrow as the only bright accent. The soft palette keeps the figure legible, and the dollar sign is high-contrast black on beige.
psychology: Sweat drops, a strained frown and a stooped posture with a sideways glance signal effort and strain. The heavy sack makes the cue about carrying a financial burden.
partnership: The title says you may be stuck in the wrong stage and that stage 3 is hardest, and the thumbnail shows a staircase of stages with a burdened climber, which supports the stage idea. The stage numbers are not shown, so the viewer cannot tell which stage the climber is on.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the three black words first, then the straining man with the dollar sack, then the stairs and the red arrow.
art: Clean vector cartoon with consistent outlines and cartoon shading. The man, sack and steps are coherent in perspective, and the white background is empty, so the picture is legible on a small screen.
strength: A man struggling up steps with a dollar sack explains stages and burden in one picture.
weakness: The three headline words are a plain topic label with no number, claim or question.
bottleneck: Missing stage numbers on the steps leave the staircase metaphor unquantified.
action: Hypothesis: add numerals 1, 2 and 3 on the steps with the third step highlighted, to test whether the title's hardest-stage idea becomes visible.

scene: A large glass hourglass stands on white. The upper bulb is packed with green banknotes and coins that pour as a narrow stream through the neck onto a man in a navy suit and glasses below. He is buried to the chest in a pile of cash and coins with both fists raised and his mouth wide open. A red banner reading TIME'S UP in white capitals stretches across the lower bulb.
mechanism: An hourglass filled with money pours onto a man who is being buried in it, which combines a dollar target with a time-running-out cue.
composition: The hourglass is centred and runs from the headline to the bottom edge, with the man's panicked face at the lower centre and the red banner in front of his chest. White space on both sides isolates the single subject, and the money pile spills over the bottom.
typography: Five tokens in two blocks: THE $2M TRAP in heavy black capitals across the top and TIME'S UP in white on a red banner. Both survive at 160x90. The $2M figure and the time limit are not in the title.
colors: White ground with black headline, saturated green money and a red banner as the only warm accent. The red is the alarm signal, and the green fills the bulb and the pile.
psychology: The man's open mouth, wide eyes and raised fists are alarm cues. The falling money and the banner TIME'S UP add urgency.
partnership: The title says a savings account is a silent tax, while the thumbnail talks about a two-million trap and time running out, with no savings account, interest or tax cue. The two share the money theme only, so the thumbnail does not clearly answer the title.
scan: ANALYST_VISUAL_HEURISTIC: the black THE $2M TRAP headline first, then the red TIME'S UP banner, then the man's panicked face under the money stream.
art: Clean vector cartoon with a translucent glass effect on the hourglass and a dense money pile. The money texture is detailed but coherent, the banner overlaps the glass cleanly, and the white background keeps the layout clear on mobile.
strength: A single hourglass with money and a panicked man delivers urgency and a dollar figure with a very simple layout.
weakness: The imagery and the figure have no visible link to a savings account or tax, which the title is about.
bottleneck: The title and thumbnail promise different topics, so a viewer who clicks for one may not recognise the other.
action: Hypothesis: replace the bulb money with a bank passbook and a small percent sign draining down, to test whether a savings-specific symbol aligns the picture with the title.
counterexample: Seq 20 tells a similar money-trap story but crowds the frame with many people and labels, while this row keeps one subject.
expression_label: open mouth, wide eyes, raised fists
